about.title: Newman Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Newman is a small community, and many residents travel outside city limits for specialized medical care, which can add layers of complexity when something goes wrong during treatment. Whether the harm happened at a local clinic or a larger facility in Stanislaus County, medical malpractice cases hinge on proving that a provider departed from an accepted standard of care — not simply that an outcome was disappointing. These cases move on strict legal clocks and typically require a qualified medical expert to support the claim, so early action matters. We listen to what happened, review your medical records, and evaluate whether a viable claim exists. There's no cost for this initial review, and we handle cases on contingency, meaning we're paid only if your case results in a recovery. Reaching out costs nothing and starts the clock working in your favor instead of against you.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Evidence Matter So Much

items.title: MICRA's Tight Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to file a medical malpractice claim. Missing either deadline can end a claim before it starts, so early review matters.

items.title: The 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before a lawsuit can be filed, California law requires giving the healthcare provider 90 days' advance notice of the intent to sue. Our team is familiar with this step and can help make sure it's done correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Testimony Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A poor result alone doesn't prove malpractice — California law requires a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was actually violated. We can help evaluate whether the facts support that showing.

items.question: How do I know if what happened to me was actually malpractice?
items.answer: A bad outcome by itself isn't enough under California law — the question is whether the provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard. We can review your records and help determine whether that standard was breached, often working with a qualified medical expert.

items.question: Does Newman being a smaller community affect my case?
items.answer: Not in terms of your legal rights, but it may mean your treatment happened across multiple providers or facilities outside Stanislaus County, which can affect where records need to be gathered. We can help sort out which providers and locations are relevant to your claim.

items.question: How long do I actually have to bring a claim?
items.answer: Under MICRA, it's generally one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the injury, but never more than three years from when it occurred. There's also a required 90-day notice period before filing suit, so it's best not to wait to have your situation reviewed.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We provide a free case review, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your case results in a recovery.
